## Findings
- claim-1: The original conjecture asserts minimality of both Theorem 5.4 families for each type-\(A\) bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L14-L21|claim=ordinary-document] [source-6@L24-L33|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: Bigrassmannians satisfy \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\), \(t>r+s-n\); \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is the integral Grassmannian presentation, and the lower-adjoined family generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-195] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-3: Put \(q=n-r\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). Then \(q\ge i\ge1\), \(r\ge j\ge1\), \(q-i=n-r-s+t-1\ge0\), and \(r-j=t-1\ge0\). For \[ (r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee,n)=(q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n)=(n-r,n-s,n-r-s+t,n), \] one has \[ 1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n,\qquad t^\vee>r^\vee+s^\vee-n, \] and \[ (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b). \]
- claim-4: For \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), \[ \omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r} \] integrally: \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\) iff \(\lambda'\subseteq r^q\). Thus \(\omega\) induces a graded integral ring isomorphism \[ \Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}. \] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- claim-5: With the accepted interval descriptions, \[ \omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee},\qquad \omega(G_R(v))=G_L(v^\vee). \] Indeed, \[ ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})'=(j^i,b^a), \] so conjugation maps \[ \{\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\} \] bijectively to \[ \{\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}. \] If \(a=0\), these are respectively the singleton shapes \(i^j\) and \(j^i\).
- claim-6: The induced map \[ J_v/A_+J_v\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee} \] is integral and graded, since \(\omega(A_+)=A_+\). The accepted lower-family basis certificate `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1` therefore transfers to an integral basis represented by \(G_R(v)\). Hence no proper subfamily of \(G_L(v)\) or \(G_R(v)\) generates \(J_v\).
- claim-7: Minimal generation in the Grassmannian contraction is equivalent to minimal generation of the original flag-variety basic ideal \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 207-211]
## Strategy
Independent adversarial audit of `research-attempt-research-plan-task-334-1` and dependencies `228`, `229`, `286`, `296`, `301` verifies the requested transfer.

For \(q=n-r\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\),
\[
q-i=n-r-s+t-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,
\]
so \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\), and
\[
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j).
\]
For
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee,n)=(q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n)=(q,n-s,n-r-s+t,n),
\]
one has
\[
1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n,\qquad
t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0,
\]
and direct substitution gives
\[
(i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b).
\]

Using \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), conjugation bijects partitions in \(q^r\) with those in \(r^q\); hence, integrally and weight-preservingly,
\[
\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}.
\]
Thus it induces a graded integral ring isomorphism of Grassmannian quotients. The interval-shape identities
\[
(i^j)'=j^i,\qquad ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})'=(j^i,b^a)
\]
give
\[
\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee},\qquad \omega(G_R(v))=G_L(v^\vee).
\]
For \(a=0\), both intervals are singleton intervals \(i^j\) and \(j^i\), so the same conclusion holds.

Because \(\omega(A_+)=A_+\), this descends to an integral graded isomorphism
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\cong J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
The accepted lower-family basis certificate `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1` therefore transfers to \(G_R(v)\); \(G_L(v)\) is already an integral quotient basis. A proper subfamily cannot span its quotient basis and hence cannot generate \(J_v\). Finally, minimality transfers from the Grassmannian contraction back to the original flag-variety basic ideal by [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 207-211].

The requested original two-family minimality conjecture is established. No universal transition identity is asserted.
